phase-summary.outcome: `game.ts` no longer owns the first-layer branch logic for core action families. Navigation, social, combat, inventory, and rune-forge action handling now live in dedicated engine action modules, and the extracted runtime path starts using `narrativeStatDelta` and item `narrativeStatDelta` instead of pushing the trait/feature split deeper into engine code.

changes.change: Added `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/engine/actions/navigation.ts`, `social.ts`, `combat.ts`, `inventory.ts`, `rune-forge.ts`, and shared `action-types.ts` so action availability and perform logic are no longer authored inline in `game.ts`.

Rewired `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/engine/game.ts` to compose those modules for `availabilityForAction`, `performAction`, prepared spell execution, forge craft, and forge evolution while keeping `GameEngine` as orchestration.

Added shared `applyNarrativeStatDelta()` in `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/engine/game-runtime-helpers.ts` and changed final action application so `ActionOutcome` carries `narrativeStatDelta` instead of separate trait/feature payloads.

Renamed runtime inventory item stat payloads from `traitDelta` to `narrativeStatDelta` in `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/core/types.ts`, `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/engine/game-entity-factories.ts`, `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/engine/game.ts`, and `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/replay/harness.ts`.

verification.command: pnpm --dir docs-site exec vitest run tests/unit/game-engine.test.ts

follow-ups.item: `62-03` and `62-04` completed the remaining extraction/normalization follow-through, so the action-family split no longer carries the stale `game.ts` ownership caveats noted during the initial rollout.

Historical deed/dialogue/content-schema surfaces still intentionally carry some `traitDelta` / `featureDelta` naming where the content model owns the shape; the runtime-owned seams stay on `narrativeStatDelta`.
